items.title: Government to remove two-year tax rule on lump sum death benefits in Budget 26
items.summary: According to Professional Pensions, the UK government will scrap the rule taxing pension death benefits paid more than two years after a member's death, effective from 28 October 2026.

items.title: Financial sector gives mixed reaction to Budget 2026 tax and spending measures
items.summary: According to Investment Week, fund managers and analysts have responded cautiously to Chancellor John Healey’s first Budget, welcoming the retention of the cash Isa allowance while criticising hikes to bank and savings taxes.

items.title: Biba welcomes IPT freeze in Budget but calls for long-term reduction
items.summary: According to Insurance Age, the British Insurance Brokers’ Association has welcomed the Chancellor’s decision to leave the insurance premium tax rate untouched, but urged the government to commit to a freeze.

items.title: Global mining insurance capacity grows, but supply chain and cyber risks rise
items.summary: According to Insurance Business, willis reports record mining insurance capacity and rate reductions, warning that risks like critical mineral supply chains and operational cyber threats are becoming increasingly interconnected.

items.title: Government announces £100 winter energy payment for England
items.summary: According to BBC, up to 20 million households in England will receive a £100 payment funded by a temporary rise in the bank corporation tax surcharge.

items.title: Budget 2026: Energy payments, Isa rules and minimum wage changes announced
items.summary: According to BBC, chancellor John Healey has delivered his maiden Budget, introducing household energy payments funded by a bank tax rise, scrapping planned cash Isa cuts, and lifting the minimum wage.
